subject: Biology
description: Male/female anatomy, fertilisation, hormones, common terms, contraception

questions.stem: The female gametes are produced in the:

options.option_text: Ovaries (paired, located in the pelvic cavity)

questions.explanation: Ovaries — produce ova (egg cells) by oogenesis; release one mature ovum per menstrual cycle (typically days 12-16). Uterus = womb (where embryo implants and develops). Fallopian tubes = oviducts where fertilisation typically occurs. Cervix = lower opening of uterus connecting to vagina. Ovaries also secrete hormones — oestrogen + progesterone — controlling the menstrual cycle and pregnancy.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Fertilisation in humans normally takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Fertilisation occurs in the AMPULLARY region of the fallopian tube (the wider segment closer to the ovary). Sperm travel from vagina → cervix → uterus → fallopian tube; fertilise the egg released from the ovary at ovulation. The resulting zygote moves down the tube over ~5-7 days, dividing → blastocyst → implants in the uterus' endometrium. Implantation = pregnancy onset. IVF (in-vitro fertilisation) bypasses the tube — fertilisation happens in a petri dish, then transferred to uterus.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The male sex hormone responsible for development of secondary sexual characters is:
questions.explanation: Testosterone — produced by Leydig cells of the testes (also small amount by adrenal cortex). Drives secondary male characters at puberty: facial/body hair, deeper voice, muscle mass, growth spurt, sperm production. Stimulated by LH from anterior pituitary. Female hormones — Oestrogen (breast development, menstrual cycle, body fat distribution) + Progesterone (pregnancy maintenance, milk production prep) — secreted by ovaries.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Average duration of human pregnancy from last menstrual period (LMP) is:
questions.explanation: Pregnancy = 40 weeks (~9 months 7 days) from first day of LMP. Calculated using Naegele's rule. Trimesters — 1st (1-13 wk), 2nd (14-26), 3rd (27-40). Term pregnancy: 37-42 weeks. Pre-term: <37; post-term: >42. Critical milestones: heartbeat detectable ~6-7 wk via ultrasound; quickening (movement felt) ~16-20 wk; viability ~24 wk. Newer 'gestational age' calculation from ultrasound is more accurate than LMP-based.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The chromosomal complement of a normal human zygote is:

options.option_text: 46 chromosomes (diploid; 23 pairs including XX or XY)

questions.explanation: Egg (n=23, haploid) + Sperm (n=23, haploid) → Zygote (2n=46, diploid). 22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes. Female XX, Male XY. Sperm decides the sex (since XX mother gives X always; XY father gives X or Y). Trisomy 21 (extra chromosome 21) = Down syndrome. Klinefelter (XXY) — male, infertile. Turner (XO) — female, single X, short stature. Down screen during pregnancy via NIPT (cell-free fetal DNA).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The pituitary hormone that triggers OVULATION in females is:
questions.explanation: Anterior pituitary releases TWO gonadotropins: FSH (stimulates follicle growth in ovary, day 1-13) and LH (LH surge ~day 13-14 → triggers ovulation). After ovulation, LH supports the corpus luteum (which secretes progesterone). Prolactin (anterior pituitary) — milk production. Oxytocin (posterior pituitary) — uterine contractions during labour + milk ejection during breastfeeding ('let-down reflex'). Hypothalamus → GnRH → pituitary → FSH/LH → ovary → estrogen/progesterone — the HPG axis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The human placenta serves which TWO main functions?

options.option_text: Nutrient/gas/waste exchange between mother and foetus + endocrine (hormone) function

questions.explanation: Placenta — temporary organ, develops from chorion (foetal) + endometrium (maternal). Functions: (1) EXCHANGE — O₂, glucose, amino acids cross to foetus; CO₂, urea cross back to mother. (2) ENDOCRINE — secretes hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin — basis of pregnancy test, peaks ~10 wk), oestrogen, progesterone, hPL (human placental lactogen). (3) Barrier — partial; many drugs/viruses cross (Zika, rubella, alcohol, nicotine). Expelled as 'afterbirth' minutes after delivery.
